Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
36-year-old man with 4-day history of severe headache, subjective fever, generalized myalgias, and diffuse blanching pruritic rash after recent travel to Thailand; arboviral infection (dengue vs. chikungunya) highest on differential, meningitis and malaria must be ruled out. Urgent in-person assessment advised today.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Severe continuous headache x4 days → subjective fever followed within same 24 h; rash appeared subsequently.  
• Associated symptoms: Generalized muscle aches; feels cold. Denies photophobia, neck stiffness, vomiting, cough/coryza, earache, focal weakness, paresthesias, joint swelling.  
• Pertinent negatives: No shivering/rigors, no non-blanching rash, no bleeding, no retro-orbital pain reported.  
• Past medical/surgical history: None.  
• Medications: Paracetamol and ibuprofen PRN with poor relief.  
• Allergies: None known.  
• Social/travel: Returned from Thailand 1 week ago; multiple mosquito bites; travel companion also unwell. No other social history obtained.  
• Preventive: Not discussed.

Examination:
(Remote video; no vitals)  
• Skin: Diffuse red itchy rash; blanches on glass test.  
• Neurologic: No focal deficits elicited on history.  
• ENT/eyes: No photophobia reported.  
• Neck: No self-reported stiffness.  
• Other systems: Not examined.

Impression:
Most likely:  
1. Dengue fever – compatible travel, fever, severe headache, myalgias, blanching rash day 3-5.  
2. Chikungunya virus infection – similar arbovirus; rash and systemic symptoms, though severe arthralgia absent.  
Must exclude:  
3. Malaria (P. falciparum) – endemic exposure; fever/headache; rash atypical but serious if missed.  
4. Viral meningitis – less likely given lack of photophobia/neck stiffness and blanching rash, but considered.  
(Transcript and DDx consistent; no conflicts.)

Plan:
• Urgent same-day in-person GP hub assessment for full physical exam, vital signs, and point-of-care tests.  
• Possible escalation to hospital for:  
  – Full blood count, platelets, LFTs, dengue NS1/serology, malaria thick/thin films, blood cultures.  
  – Lumbar puncture if meningitis suspected after exam.  
• Continue paracetamol/ibuprofen for comfort unless contraindicated.  
• Safety-net advice: If unable to obtain urgent appointment, go directly to emergency department. Seek immediate care for worsening headache, confusion, neck stiffness, non-blanching or bleeding rash, persistent vomiting, or high fever.  
• Follow-up: Telephone update after in-person review or within 24 h to discuss results/next steps.

Quality checks:

● Missing expected elements: Objective vitals, detailed neuro exam, full social history (smoking/alcohol), immunization/travel prophylaxis history, documentation of follow-up arrangement contact details.  
● Conflicts: None noted between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: Generally clear; occasional incomplete sentences, no vital signs or physical findings obtainable via telehealth.
